a: Omarchy is AI-first: pick your coding agent once and everything AI (this helper's chat, crash diagnosis, SUPER+A) uses it. Open the menu with SUPER+SPACE, go to Setup → Default agent, and choose (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini…). Or in a terminal: omarchy default agent claude. Then sign in to the agent once and you're set.

SUPER (the Windows key) runs everything. SUPER+SPACE opens the Omarchy menu — apps, install, style, setup, power. SUPER+K shows every keybinding on your machine, including your own custom ones. When lost, press SUPER+K.
SUPER+RETURN opens a terminal. SUPER+SHIFT+RETURN opens the browser (and SUPER+ALT+RETURN opens tmux). Or press SUPER+SPACE and type any app's name, like a search bar.

SUPER+C copies, SUPER+V pastes, SUPER+X cuts — the same keys in every app, including the terminal (no more Ctrl+Shift+C gymnastics). SUPER+CTRL+V opens your clipboard history so you can paste something from earlier.

SUPER+W closes the focused window (many apps here have no titlebar buttons — this is the way). Hold SUPER and drag with the left mouse button to move a floating window; SUPER + right-button drag resizes it.

SUPER+SPACE → Install → Package for official software, or Install → AUR for community packages (huge selection, unvetted — like npm). Type the name, it fuzzy-finds. Remove later via SUPER+SPACE → Remove → Package, which also cleans config and dependencies.

q: Turn a website into an app
a: SUPER+SPACE → Install → Web App. Give it a name, the URL, and an icon — Omarchy wraps the site as a real app with its own window and launcher entry. Great for Gmail, WhatsApp Web, YouTube, dashboards. This is how several of the preinstalled 'apps' work.

Independent desks for separate contexts — browser on one, work on another. SUPER+1…9 jumps to a workspace (they're created as you visit them). SUPER+SHIFT+1…9 sends the focused window to that workspace. The numbers in your top bar show which desk you're on.

SUPER+arrow keys move focus between windows in the direction you press. SUPER+SHIFT+arrows swap the windows themselves. New windows tile automatically — nothing overlaps unless it's a floating window.

A hidden overlay workspace: press SUPER+S and it drops over whatever you're doing; press SUPER+S again and it's gone — but everything in it keeps running. Send any window there with SUPER+ALT+S. Perfect for a terminal, music player, or chat you want one keypress away.

q: Make a window fill the screen
a: SUPER+F expands the focused window within the layout; SUPER+CTRL+F is true fullscreen (bar hidden). Press the same key again to go back. Exact behavior can vary if customized — SUPER+K shows what yours does.

SUPER+SPACE → Style → Theme. One choice restyles everything at once — colors, bar, terminal, lock screen, wallpaper. Omarchy ships many themes and you can install more from git URLs (Style → Theme → Install). Backgrounds cycle with SUPER+CTRL+SPACE.

Brightness usually lives on your keyboard's function keys. Display settings (resolution, scaling, arrangement) are in SUPER+SPACE → Setup → Monitors — it edits the config for you. Night-light and idle/lock timing are under Setup too.
SUPER+SPACE → Setup → Wi-Fi opens the network picker; Setup → Bluetooth pairs devices. Both also sit as icons in the top bar — click them for the same panels.

Press PRINT — select an area, and it opens in a small editor for arrows/text before saving to your Pictures folder (and the clipboard). SUPER+CTRL+PRINT grabs TEXT from anywhere on screen via OCR — great for copying from images or videos.

SUPER+SPACE → Update. It updates Omarchy itself plus all packages in one go. Omarchy versions arrive as regular package updates — no reinstalls. If something looks odd after an update, the same menu has Update → Config restore options.
SUPER+SPACE → Power has lock, suspend, restart, and shutdown. The screen locks automatically after idle (timing under Setup → Idle). Closing the laptop lid suspends by default.

If a program crashes, Omarchy notices and shows a notification offering an AI diagnosis — click it and your default agent investigates the crash for you. Nothing set up? It only appears once you've chosen your default agent (see 'Set up your AI agent').
